title: Growth wins, gaps, and manager ask playbook (personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose / quick note to self:
- This doc is my scratchpad to pull together: recent impact, gaps I want to close, concrete asks for manager conversations, and a 6–12 week stretch plan.
- Keep it informal; use it before 1:1s, review prep, and calibration chats.

Recent wins (evidence + why it mattered):
- Reduced average requisition-to-offer time from ~48d to 33d for backend infra roles (Jan–Feb 2026). How: tightened hiring committee turnaround, implemented daily update cadence with hiring PMs, tracked candidate stage TLs in lightweight sheet.
  - Evidence: hiring-metrics sheet linked; 3 hires converted in <30d.
  - Business impact: reduced offer fall-through; engineering onboarding ramped up faster for Serving Runtime team.

- Piloted interview-loop rubric for Platform Eng (beta with 6 interviewers). Outcome: interviewer calibration score variance down 18% (internal survey).
  - Follow-up: scale rubric + 1-pager for interviewers; integrate into hiring-trainings doc.

- Launched 'first 90 days' onboarding checklist for Dedicated team; removed 6 manual steps and automated welcome links via HR-bot. New hire satisfaction improved in NPS pulse (+0.4).

Gaps / things to own / improvement areas (quick, candid):
- Up-level data hygiene: candidate / offer reason tags inconsistent. Need a one-off clean and automated normalization (work with Recruiting ops).
- Proactively influence leader hiring forecast — often too reactive. Need to embed monthly HC check-ins with GTM and Product leads.
- Coaching bandwidth: I want to spend more time on high-impact 1:1s but feel pulled into meetings. Need to protect deep-focus time.

Short list of metrics I want to show in my next review (with current status):
- Time-to-offer median: 33d (goal 30d by end of Q2).
- Offer-accept rate: 78% (goal 85%).
- Interviewer calibration variance: -18% vs baseline (goal -30%).
- New-hire 90-day ramp health: 72% 'on track' (goal 85%).

Manager ask (concrete, scripted):
- Big ask: 0.2 FTE recurring allocation for Recruiting Operations (either temporary contractor or reallocate internal headcount) for Q2–Q4 to fix data hygiene and automation backlog.
  - Why: freeing me from repetitive data cleanup will create 1.5–2 days/week net for strategic hiring forecast work and coach time.
  - What success looks like: normalized candidate tags, automated offer reasons, saved ~5 hours/week across team.

- Ask follow-ups:
  1) Quarterly alignment slot with Product + GTM leads to collect hiring priorities (30–45m, calendar hold).
  2) Permission to run a 6-week pilot of interviewer calibration sessions (biweekly) with applied interview feedback loop and compensation for interviewers (swag / small thank-you).

6–12 week stretch plan (specific to next 1:1s and review cycle):
- Week 1–2: run a 2-hour data-cleaning session with Recruiting Ops (deliverable: cleaned normalized dataset + mapping doc).
- Week 3–4: build simple dashboard (sheet + one-pager) of the 4 metrics above and circulate to Hiring leads.
- Week 5–8: run pilot interviewer calibration sessions; collect survey data; create playbook for scale.
- Week 9–12: run hiring forecast alignment meeting pilot with 3 cross-functional partners; document cadence and sample agenda.

Example talking points for next 1:1 (short bullets):
- "Priority update: closed gap on TtO to 33d — next target 30d; blocked by data hygiene and inconsistent offer reason tags."
- "Proposal: 0.2 FTE for Recruiting Ops to automate normalization and free capacity for strategic hires — I can draft a scope and ROI for your review."
- "Requesting permission to run a 6-week interviewer calibration pilot and to book a recurring monthly HC forecast meeting with Product/GTM."

Potential objections I might hear and my rebuttals (prep):
- Objection: "We can't spare budget/headcount."
  - Rebuttal: "Short-term contractor for 12 weeks reduces time-to-hire and increases offer-accept rate; cost of unfilled role > contractor cost — I'll model the math and show expected delta."
- Objection: "Managers won't attend another meeting."
  - Rebuttal: "Make it 30–40 minutes focused on decisions (priorities + blockers) and rotate invite list; I will own the agenda and notes and show immediate quick wins."

Wildcards / stretch outcomes I'd love to drive (longer term):
- Standardized interviewer training across Eng/Product, leading to a 25% interviewer variance reduction and better predictive hiring outcomes.
- A small internal hiring automation (scripts + glue) that saves 10–15 hours/week across recruiting and people ops.

Quick TODOs (scratch, actionable):
- [ ] Draft 0.2 FTE scope + cost model (by next Tue).
- [ ] Clean candidate tags for Jan–Feb dataset (session w/ Jonah on Thu).
- [ ] Build dashboard skeleton (sheet + 4 charts) by Feb 26.
- [ ] Draft pilot invite template for calibration sessions and send to Maya for feedback.

Notes to self about tone / calibration in manager convo:
- Be concise: open with one-line impact statement, then the ask + ROI. Avoid granular operational asks in first minute.
- Bring evidence: show the dashboard or one slide with 3 numbers.
- Offer a low-friction trial: finite pilot with clear end date and measurable success criteria.

Random ideas / brain-dump (may be useful later):
- Micro-incentives for interviewers (meal vouchers, slack recognition, quarterly top-interviewer list).
- Office hours (1x month) for hiring managers to ask quick questions — reduce ad-hoc interruptions.
- Embed a short one-question 'was the interview relevant?' at the end of loop to collect quick signal from interviewers (alpha test).

End of scratchpad. Keep tidy; will move bits into a formal PRD if management approves the 0.2 FTE pilot and calibration program.
